messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for canary model canary-v3 in eu-west-1. p95 ~450ms -> 1.8s, p99 ~2.9s -> 5.4s. Streaming stalls increasing, ~12% streams experiencing stalls. Auto-page: oncall@sara.

sara (oncall): ack. I'm looking. Anyone seeing traffic changes?

alex (infra): seeing elevated CPU on canary pool nodes (gpu-2.*). KV-cache miss rate jumped from 4% -> 38% on canary-v3. Logs show a sudden tokenization mismatch on warmup requests.

maria (support): We got a ticket from AcmePayments complaining about slow responses and timeouts around 12:03 UTC. They're on eu-west-1.

sara (oncall): tagging @vikram (oncall-next) for handoff if this gets noisy. First goal: mitigate customer impact. Any quick mitigations?

alex (infra): possible quick wins: 1) shift canary traffic back to baseline model v2, 2) force kv cache warmup (but that's heavy), 3) temporarily increase replica count for canary to reduce queueing. Recommend traffic shift to baseline by 20-50% immediately.

sara (oncall): agree. Initiating partial traffic shift 40% away from canary-v3 -> baseline-v2. Using infra tool.

deploy-bot: /traffic-shift --target canary-v3 --region eu-west-1 --to baseline-v2 --percent 40 --reason "mitigate p99 spike"

deploy-bot: Traffic shift started. Estimated completion ~30s.

alex (infra): confirming: after shift, CPU on canary nodes down ~30%, KV-cache miss % dropping as rate reduces.

maria (support): messaging AcmePayments: "We're seeing elevated latency in a canary rollout and have shifted traffic to a stable model to mitigate. We'll follow up in 30 mins."

sara (oncall): good. Let's monitor p95/p99 and streaming stall rate. If not stable in 10m, escalate rollback.

(2m later)

incident-bot: METRIC UPDATE: p99 eu-west-1 canary-v3 = 3.1s -> 2.0s after shift; streaming stall rate down 12% -> 4%.

vikram (oncall-next): I can take handoff in 15m. If you think we need a full rollback, I'll coordinate.

alex (infra): digging logs: tokenization change in model artifacts causes KV keys to differ (prefix length trimmed). Sample log: ```
[2026-03-15T12:05:22Z] model-loader: checksum ok
[2026-03-15T12:05:22Z] tokenizer: variant=trim_prefix=true
[2026-03-15T12:05:22Z] kv-cache: key_hash miss_ratio=0.38
```

sara (oncall): ok that's helpful. That explains cache churn + backend work. For safety, I'm going to request a full rollback of canary-v3 in eu-west-1 and stop the rollout. We already shifted 40% traffic; rollback will restore prior stable routing.

deploy-bot: /rollback --model canary-v3 --region eu-west-1 --confirm "rollback due to kv-cache regression and p99 spike"
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated. Expected duration 2min.

incident-bot: Paging oncall-alert: paging sara to confirm rollback complete.

(rollback completes)

deploy-bot: Rollback complete: canary-v3 -> stable routing restored. All traffic now on baseline-v2 in eu-west-1.

incident-bot: METRIC UPDATE: p95=420ms, p99=480ms, streaming stalls ~0.8%. Back to baseline.

maria (support): notifying AcmePayments: "Issue mitigated, traffic reverted to prior model. We're investigating root cause and will share ETA for fix."

sara (oncall): handing off to @vikram for post-mortem and RCA. Key notes for handoff:
- Trigger: canary-v3 tokenization change (trim_prefix) caused kv-cache key mismatch -> cache churn -> CPU + tail latency.
- Impact: eu-west-1 p99 spike, streaming stalls, ~12% of streams impacted during peak window; 1 enterprise customer reported timeouts but no data loss.
- Mitigation: partial traffic shift (40%) then full rollback; rollback completed, metrics normalized.
- Actions in flight: infra to add canary-level cache-warmup before rollout OR ensure tokenizer config pinned across rollout artifacts.

vikram (oncall-next): taking handoff. I'll coordinate with infra + model infra to block further rollout until we have a patch. Also will open escalation with model team to revert tokenizer config and add preflight checks.

alex (infra): planned immediate follow-ups: 1) add a preflight check that verifies tokenizer config/flags match baseline for canary rollouts, 2) add a kv-cache warmup job for canaries that runs a synthetic prefix set for 5 minutes, 3) add telemetry alert for sudden kv-cache miss jumps.

sara (oncall): adding to incident timeline and creating incident doc. ETA for RCA meeting 3h. Maria, please send customer follow-up note after RCA.

maria (support): will do. Drafting message: "We've reverted the canary rollout that caused latency spikes. Root cause appears to be tokenizer config drift causing cache misses; we'll have a full RCA in ~3hrs and will follow up with specific remediation and timeline."

(closure)

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. No ongoing customer outages. Handoff: vikram (oncall-next). Follow-ups: RCA meeting scheduled; infra/model teams assigned.

vikram (oncall-next): acknowledged. I'll take this from here. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
